current.headline: Hiragana: the 46 sounds that build Japanese
current.summary: Forty-six characters, arranged in a neat grid of vowels and consonants. Learn the pattern and the whole script falls into place, a row at a time.

text.t: Hiragana is the first script every Japanese child learns, and it is the one you will read most. Every word in Japanese can be written in hiragana, even when it is usually written in kanji. Children's books are written almost entirely in it.
There are 46 basic characters. That may sound like a lot, but they follow a grid that makes them far easier to learn than 46 random shapes.
Every row starts with a consonant, and every column is one of the five vowels: a, i, u, e, o. Read across a row and you get that consonant with each vowel in turn.

current.headline: Kanji without fear: what they are and how to read them
current.summary: There are thousands of kanji, but you do not learn them all at once, and you never learn them alone. Here is why Japanese still uses them, and how readings actually work.

text.t: Kanji are the characters Japanese borrowed from Chinese, starting around 1,500 years ago. Each one carries a meaning, and most also carry a sound. A newspaper uses around 2,000 of them regularly. That number scares people, so let's put it in proportion.

You do not need 2,000 kanji to read this paper. Every kanji here comes with furigana, the small readings printed above it, until you choose to turn them off. You will meet kanji one word at a time, in sentences you understand.
Some of the simplest kanji began as drawings.
(tree): a person leaning against a tree. Not every kanji has a story that neat, but many have a part that hints at meaning and another that hints at sound.
Japanese has a lot of words that sound the same. Written in kana, they look the same too. Kanji tell them apart at a glance.

note.t: In speech, pitch and context separate them. In writing, kanji do.

text.t: Kanji also make text faster to read. Japanese does not put spaces between words, so the switch between kanji and hiragana shows where words begin and end.
